messages:
Mike B: FYI escalated ticket from AcmeCorp — their app keeps getting a 400 from our function-caller when calling payment/invoice tools. They say "tool_choice" picked `generate_invoice` instead of `lookup_invoice` and the payload shape doesn't match so schema validation fails.
Alex Chen: can you paste the original request body / model response?
Mike B: from customer console logs: ```json
{
  "input": "get invoice 9371",
  "functions": ["lookup_invoice", "generate_invoice"],
  "tool_choice": "generate_invoice"
}
```
Katie R: oof, tool_choice picking generator vs lookup will definitely break args. do we have the model raw function call (name + args)?
Mike B: yes, here's the model call we got back: ```json
{
  "name": "generate_invoice",
  "arguments": {
    "customer_name": "Acme",
    "line_items": [{"desc": "service", "amt": 120}],
    "billing_cycle": "monthly"
  }
}
```
Sarah L: the lookup tool expects `{ invoice_id: string }` only. generate_invoice has a completely different schema. no wonder validation fails with 422.
Support Bot: Incident Alert - function-caller returned schema_validation_error for thread 1765201234 (count: 6)
Mike B: customer sees: `400 Bad Request - function call schema mismatch: missing field invoice_id`
Alex Chen: quick check: is there ambiguity in tool naming? both tools live in the same namespace `invoice.*`?
Mike B: in their integration they register functions as `invoice_lookup` and `invoice_generate` but our tool router maps to `lookup_invoice` and `generate_invoice` (we canonicalize). seems okay but there was a recent merge that added fuzzy aliasing for synonyms.
Katie R: aha — fuzzy aliasing. I remember an opt-in feature: "tool_choice synonyms" that maps plain text to tools. if the model said "create invoice" it might map to generate even when the user asked to "get invoice" due to poor lemmatization.
Alex Chen: can we see the router decision log? the trace should indicate why the model choice was overridden (if it was).
Mike B: snippet from router logs: ```
[2026-02-18T14:12:33Z] model_choice=generate_invoice, alias_score=0.72, fuzzy_overrode=false, final_tool=generate_invoice
[2026-02-18T14:12:33Z] schema_validation: expected invoice_id -> failed
```
Sarah L: weird that fuzzy_overrode=false but alias_score 0.72. maybe threshold changed?
Alex Chen: I pushed a config change last week to lower alias threshold for multi-word commands to 0.7 to improve UX. looks like this crossed the threshold.
Katie R: so root cause: threshold change allowed synonym match for "get invoice" -> generate_invoice. customer intent was lookup, not create.
Mike B: customer is upset, says this broke billing flow and they got wrong charges in staging. they want a repro and fix timeline.
Alex Chen: repro steps I used: 1) send user prompt "get invoice 9371" 2) include registered functions lookup/generate 3) get model function call -> generate_invoice 4) function-caller validates against generate schema -> ok (but wrong) OR fails if args mismatch.
Katie R: can you share the exact model prompt/response we used?
Alex Chen: here's the model reply raw: ```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": null,
  "function_call": {
    "name": "generate_invoice",
    "arguments": "{\"customer_name\": \"Acme\", \"line_items\": [{\"desc\": \"service\", \"amt\":120}]}"
  }
}
```
Mike B: customer also included a tool manifest that declares `lookup_invoice` docs first. might be an ordering issue.
Sarah L: two mitigations: 1) revert alias threshold change -> immediate mitigation; 2) strengthen schema validation to check allowed call contexts (e.g., generate should never be suggested for one-word queries with invoice id pattern).
Alex Chen: agree. I'll open a rollback PR for the threshold and add a regression test that asserts "get invoice <id>" maps to lookup.
Katie R: on the support side, reply to customer with repro steps, timeline: rollback in 1h, full fix (contextual rules + tests) by EOD. propose short-term patch to hard-block generate_invoice when prompt contains invoice id regex `\b\d{3,}\b`.
Mike B: customer wants logs we can provide: will attach model_choice traces and the function call payload. they asked for root cause summary and whether data leaked.
Sarah L: no PII in traces besides invoice id and customer name. escalations/security: flag to sec for review: @oncall (Oncall Bot) please triage if we need legal notice.
Oncall Bot: @Sarah L acknowledged. creating sec ticket SEC-4872.
Alex Chen: action items: - Alex: rollback alias threshold (inflight PR) - Katie: draft support reply + short-term patch (regex block) - Sarah: verify no leak and coordinate with sec - Mike: collect customer logs and confirm repro ok
Mike B: I'll update customer with planned rollback ETA 13:40 PST and include logs.
Katie R: quick snippet to reproduce locally (use this): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{
  "input":"get invoice 9371",
  "functions": ["lookup_invoice","generate_invoice"]
}' | jq
```
Alex Chen: I'll also add a CI test that asserts alias_score < 0.7 for "get invoice 9371" after rollback.
Mike B: customer replied: ":eyes: thanks — please confirm once fixed. we need a follow-up postmortem."
Sarah L: postmortem planned after incident closure. add to postmortems channel.
Support Bot: Incident Update - rollback deployed to canary at 2026-02-18T15:05Z (build 3547).
Katie R: can we close this thread after we've confirmed customer acceptance?
Mike B: yes. leaving open until they ack.
Alex Chen: moving to follow-up: add strict schema mapping for function-caller + a feature flag to disable fuzzy aliasing per workspace.
Sarah L: good idea — that'll let enterprise customers opt out.
Mike B: thanks team. I'll ping when customer confirms.
